In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
TDF-based first line therapy in South India is not associated with the development of resistance to AZT.
the use of TDF as a first-line therapy for HIV-1-infested patients is safe and effective.
in the present scenario of HIV-1 subtype C, K65R is a good predictor of susceptibility to AZT, and AZT can be a good choice for second-line therapy in patients failing TDF.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
in patients failing TDF, K65R is a common mutation but is associated with TAMs and M184V, which can be considered as an advantage for AZT and TDF, respectively, in second-line therapy.
, in the presence of K65R and M184V, AZT can still be considered as the second-line NRTI in the context of TDF-based second-line HAART.
, in patients who have failed TDF-based first line HAART, AZT is still a viable option for second line therapy and TDF can be considered for third line therapy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the majority of patients failing TDF based first-line HAART in South Asia have a low level of drug resistance, and therefore, the use of TDF in second-line therapy is still a reasonable option.
in most patients, AZT can still be considered for the second-line therapy.
, despite the fact that K65R mutation is a barrier to TDF use in the second-line regimen, the low prevalence of this mutation makes it feasible to use TDF in the second-line therapy.
